text:
Maya: Heading to the Prague offsite in 6 days — quick poll: window or aisle? Also packing q: I'm planning to bring a 150Wh power bank. Is that a hard no for carry-on? Any tips for toiletries (international liquids limits, toothpaste packs, customs)?

David: Window all the way for naps :zzz: but aisle if you need to stretch. For the powerbank — check with the airline. Most allow <=100Wh no questions.

Sophia: FYI the basic rule is batteries in carry-on only. >100Wh often needs airline approval; some people get away with 150Wh but YMMV. Example labels to check:```
20,000mAh / ~74Wh -> fine
50,000mAh / ~185Wh -> usually requires airline approval or not allowed
```

engbot: quick checklist: passport, boarding pass, powerbank (carry-on), liquids <=100ml each in 1L clear bag, meds (declare if needed), plug adapter, noise-cancelling headphones. :white_check_mark:

Oliver: Toothpaste packets and single-use mouthwash are amazing for overnight flights. Also compression socks + eye mask + a thin scarf (doubles as blanket). Pro tip: put valuables and a mini dopp kit in your personal item, not checked bag.

Nina: If you plan to push a 150Wh bank, call the airline now — they'll tell you if you can sign a form. For EU airports, security can be stricter than US. Keep the original packaging or a printed spec if you have it.

David: Another small trick — stick spare socks in your carry-on pocket (makes cramped plane naps way better). And ziploc for receipts/chargers on return.

Maya: Thanks all — so plan B is buy a 100Wh unit if airline says no. Poll: react with :window: for window, :aisle: for aisle, or reply with "depends". I'll book seats after tally.

engbot: NOTE: international rules vary. FAA/IATA guidance: batteries in carry-on; most countries follow similar limits. Example: https://www.iata.org/en/programs/cargo/dgr/ (worth checking).
